title: BCO 34-1 Petitions re: Missouri Presbytery
disposition_detail: Dismissed both BCO 34-1 overtures/petitions requesting that the General Assembly assume original jurisdiction over alleged doctrinal errors of TE Greg Johnson. The SJC held it lacked authority because Johnson had been removed from Missouri Presbytery's rolls under BCO 38-3a and Memorial Presbyterian Church had withdrawn, so the PCA no longer had jurisdiction over him. No merits ruling on the doctrinal allegations; vote 22-1, with M. Duncan dissenting and Lucas absent.
first_summary: The SJC dismissed two BCO 34-1 requests that the General Assembly assume original jurisdiction over TE Greg Johnson's alleged doctrinal errors. Because Memorial Presbyterian Church left the PCA and Missouri Presbytery removed Johnson from its rolls, the SJC said the PCA no longer had jurisdiction over him. It made no merits ruling.
summary: The SJC dismissed two BCO 34-1 overtures asking the General Assembly to assume original jurisdiction over alleged doctrinal errors by TE Greg Johnson. After Memorial Presbyterian Church withdrew from the PCA and Missouri Presbytery removed Johnson's name from its rolls under BCO 38-3a, the SJC held it lacked authority to assume original jurisdiction because the PCA no longer had jurisdiction over him. The dismissal did not resolve the doctrinal allegations; one commissioner dissented.

sources.supports: Case identity, BCO 34-1 procedural vehicle, deciding body, challenged action, SJC holding on lack of jurisdiction, vote, and dissent/absence.
Attached Missouri Presbytery public letter; background from Presbytery, not adopted SJC reasoning.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case No. 2022-12, BCO 34-1 Petitions re: Missouri Presbytery; SJC Decision on Petitions dated March 2, 2023, 50th GA; recommended by an SJC committee and approved 22-1 (lines 13-25; printed p. 919).
evidence_notes.dispute: Two overtures, Overture 36 from Southeast Alabama Presbytery and Overture 37 from Grace Presbytery, requested that the GA assume original jurisdiction under BCO 34-1 over alleged doctrinal errors of TE Greg Johnson (lines 19-20; printed p. 919).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC dismissed/lacked authority to assume original jurisdiction because, after Memorial Presbyterian Church withdrew and Missouri Presbytery removed Johnson from its rolls under BCO 38-3a and discontinued its BCO 31-2 investigation, the PCA no longer had jurisdiction over Johnson; no merits ruling was made (lines 21-25; printed pp. 919-920).
evidence_notes.qualifications: M. Duncan dissented; Lucas was absent; the vote was 22-1 (lines 25, 27, 31; printed pp. 919-920). The Presbytery public letter is attached background and not adopted SJC reasoning (line 23; lines 32-54).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: None. The decision does not incorporate another decision. The attached Presbytery letter mentions prior SJC 2020-12 (line 46), but the SJC did not rely on or adopt that decision here.

source_limits: The decision is brief. It recites the jurisdictional developments and conclusion but does not analyze the merits of the doctrinal allegations or reproduce the overtures. The attached Missouri Presbytery letter (lines 32-54) states Presbytery's perspective and is not adopted as SJC reasoning.
benchmark_examples: O04 (2020-02): original-jurisdiction requests answered by reference to incorporated decisions; here the SJC instead dismissed for loss of jurisdiction, and 'by reference' is not a referral disposition.
A20 (2013-12): a dismissal label may not reflect a merits result; here dismissal rested on lack of authority after removal from PCA rolls, not on rejection of the doctrinal allegations.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the challenged action as the two BCO 34-1 overtures seeking original jurisdiction over TE Johnson's alleged doctrinal errors.
score_reasons.decision: States the SJC's dismissal and that no merits ruling was made, with the 22-1 vote and dissent/absence noted.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Explains the adopted reason: after Johnson was removed from Missouri Presbytery's rolls, the PCA no longer had jurisdiction over him, so the SJC lacked authority to assume original jurisdiction.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the useful limit that losing jurisdiction over the accused minister defeats a BCO 34-1 request without any merits resolution.
score_reasons.fidelity: Keeps the SJC decision, the attached Presbytery letter, and the prior 2020-12 reference distinct; does not convert allegations into findings.
score_reasons.economy: Includes only the procedural vehicle, events creating the jurisdictional defect, holding, and qualifications needed to understand the result.
